newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - SPENCER IN DOUBT FOR DUNEDIN TEST.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - SPENCER IN DOUBT FOR DUNEDIN TEST.

text.p: DUNEDIN, Aug 14 - A hamstring twinge at training on Thursday has placed Carlos Spencer in doubt for the All Blacks' Tri-series rugby test against Australia at Carisbrook on Saturday, NZPA reports.
The All Blacks first five-eighth hobbled off the ground during the team's final practice session before the match, prompting fears he may be forced to miss the test.
All Black coach John Hart said although the injury did not appear serious, the 21-year-old Auckland playmaker was in doubt for the match.
Team doctor John Mayhew said Spencer had a hamstring injury in the same leg last season. Today's strain could have stemmed from the old injury.

"We can't tell at the moment just how bad it is. He's walking around in no discomfort and we'll have to wait until tomorrow to see how it is. We may even have to wait until Saturday morning," Mayhew said.
Should Spencer be forced out, Andrew Mehrtens, who was the first choice first five-eighth at the start of the season, will partner halfback Justin Marshall in the inside backs.
It could also force team officials to reassess the composition of their reserves, who are expected to be named tomorrow.
"We'll give him as long as possible to recover, but if we think he can't play then we won't delay making the replacement," Hart said of Spencer.
"It's disappointing that it's happened right at the end of the last training session, but we're fortunate to have a player of Andrew's calibre waiting to slot in."

Spencer, who took over Mehrtens' position after the Cantabrian suffered a severe hamstring strain in the year's first test, against Fiji on June 14, has played in all the tests since, twice each against Argentina, Australia and the Springboks.
Hart said Spencer's misfortune happened 10 minutes before the end of the session today.
"He stepped and he felt it pull a little, so we pulled him out immediately as a precaution. Andrew went on and ran through the session."
Hart said he was optimistic of Spencer's playing chances because the strain was not in the same spot as the previous injury.
"It's too early to say whether he'll play or not play. It's not serious, it's minor but we'll decide tomorrow," he said.
